title: Rewrite a recurring dream
subtitle: Gently give a returning nightmare a new shape, while you're awake.

steps.body:
A recurring nightmare can lose its grip when you gently rewrite it while awake.

This is for a dream that keeps returning — not for fresh or raw trauma. If the memory is still raw, or you feel unsafe, this isn't the practice for right now; the Support tab is there for you.
Is this a dream that repeats — and do you feel steady enough to look at it gently? You can stop here anytime, and it will be waiting.

steps.title: In a few lines, what happens in the nightmare?
steps.body: Only as much as feels okay. You don't have to relive it — just sketch it.

steps.title: How activating is it to recall?

steps.body: That stirs something. Breathe. You're awake, here, and safe — the dream is not happening now. Go only as far as you choose.

steps.title: What's the worst feeling it leaves you with?
Now rewrite it.
steps.body: Change anything you want — the ending, what you're able to do, who arrives, how it feels. Give it a new shape, one you'd choose.
steps.placeholder: The way you'd want it to go instead…

steps.body: Read your new version once, slowly. Let it be the one you carry. Picture it as if this is simply how the dream goes now.

steps.title: Anything you want to hold onto from the new version?

exit.body: Dreams can be revised. You gave this one a different shape — and the more you rehearse the new version awake, the more it can soften in sleep.
